- La exportación PostgreSQL → SQLite crea y valida un `library.db` SQLite real; evita el archivo inválido que impedía iniciar Jellyfin.
- La exportación ya no copia ni marca a ciegas el historial de migraciones.

Verificado con Build Release, pruebas unitarias e integración real contra PostgreSQL. Requiere Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16+ y .NET 10.

## English

### 3.0.2 — Stability, integrity and safe export

- Fixes normalization of `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, and arrays before PostgreSQL writes, avoiding Npgsql errors caused by incompatible `Kind` values.

- PostgreSQL activation validates the connection before changing `database.xml`.
- Automatic backup restore was removed, and manual restore no longer replaces existing objects by default.
- Identical concurrent home-screen queries are coalesced while the cache is populated.
- PostgreSQL → SQLite export creates and validates a real SQLite `library.db`, preventing the invalid file that stopped Jellyfin from starting.
- Export no longer blindly marks or copies migration history.

Fixer output: TrackFixer + TranscodeFixer restore source CreationTimeUtc and LastWriteTimeUtc so Recently-Added stays honest (#31); dry-run stale-failure path no longer flips vanished files to Fixed; per-sidecar history fan-out via FixResult.AdditionalRecycled gives every recycled sidecar its own Restore button; subtitle-provider quota mid-run is now detected and handled quietly.

Playability: cross-checks ffprobe format_name against extension so an MKV renamed .mp3 emits container-extension-mismatch (F-213). HasTruncationMarker no longer treats the benign Truncating packet warning as truncation - that warning fires on real-world MKV cluster boundaries, MPEG-TS packet alignment, and MP4 mdat overlap on files that play fine in Jellyfin (Reddit reports: friskyapple, oogoom, moonplaza, Commercial-Camp-8052). Only File ended prematurely now counts.

TrackFixer ffmpeg command gains -fflags +genpts at input and -avoid_negative_ts make_zero at output - fixes the mpegts sample rate not set / Could not write header failure on Blu-ray-derived .m2ts sources, and lets OutputVerifier accept legitimate long-form duration drift (#39, slack widened from fixed 2 s to max(2 s, dur x 2 percent)).

Combined ffmpeg pass (#28, #32): FixTask now detects same-file AudioLanguage + SubtitleLanguage pairs before the fix loop and routes them through a new TrackFixer.FixCombinedAsync so one ffmpeg drops both categories in a single pass instead of two back-to-back remuxes. Two history rows recorded, one bin entry, both issues flip to Fixed.

SMART noise dedup: SmartHealthProbeWmi caches per-drive-letter WMI failures and SmartHealthProbe caches per-device smartctl timeout / IO / non-zero-exit failures. First failure per device per session still emits the diagnostic; subsequent failures on the same device are suppressed until restart. Addresses the Errors-tab spam on NVMe + mount-point setups (#38, #23).

Files: new read-only Jellyfin logs shortcut at the file-browser root supporting listing + per-file download so users can attach logs to bug reports; ApiKey= param renamed from api_key= for Jellyfin 10.10+ compatibility.

Diagnostics: Copy diagnostics button relabelled Report an issue (copies diagnostics + opens issue tracker in a new tab).

One binary for Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0.

Reliability hotfix: fixes the "13 files locked, nothing holding them" report class by switching every scanner/probe (ArtworkScanner, NfoScanner, TrickplayOptimizeScanner, BookProbeService, FileHasher) from File.OpenRead (default FileShare.Read blocks concurrent moves/deletes on Windows and shows up as ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION 32) to a new MediaFileHelper.OpenSharedRead helper using FileShare.ReadWrite | Delete. Also splits FixTask's catch-all "disk error" into four accurate diagnostic keys — FixTask.FileMissing (marks issue Fixed so retry stops), FixTask.FileLocked (sharing violation post-retry), FixTask.DiskFull (real ENOSPC only, HResult 112/39/28), residual FixTask.IOError; every bucket gets a new Errors-tab entry with actionable copy. Adds a 5s per-library-root probe to ScanTask so a hard-mounted dead NFS/SMB share can't hang the ThreadPool and force LXC restarts — unreachable roots are skipped with a diagnostic pointing at soft,timeo=30,retrans=3 mount flags. Cleans up Ffmpeg.Timeout noise on Blu-ray remuxes: TrackFixer's 30-min first pass no longer surfaces to Errors (only the 5-hour retry's failure does), Track.RemuxRetry diagnostic removed as it fired on the happy path. New README Uninstall section explaining the remove-repo -> uninstall -> restart sequence so Jellyfin's Update Plugins task can't race the deleteOnStartup marker. Still one binary for both Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0.

Duplicate detection rework with a per-pair confidence ladder (Exact 1.00 / Identified 0.90 / Heuristic 0.70) plus two hard vetoes (title-token Jaccard, runtime delta) that kill the GitHub #3 Futurama-specials false-positive class.

Fixes
- GitHub #3 - duplicate false positives on distinct files sharing an episode metadata slot.
- GitHub #12 - container CPU/RAM cards showed HOST numbers; now read cgroup v2 -> v1 first and fall through to /proc only when unbounded.
- GitHub #6 + #12-SMART - Linux SMART reported Unknown forever on drives whose libraries live on a partition; now walks partition -> disk via lsblk.
- ArtworkFixer clears the item's ImageInfos BEFORE deleting the file on disk so /Items/{id}/Images/Primary stops 404-ing after a corrupt-artwork sweep.
- Dry-run is now airtight: MissingSubtitleFixer no longer queries external subtitle providers under dry-run (was leaking which files exist and burning provider quota).
- Field report A1: default-threaded ffmpeg pinned every core on a 1-2 vCPU Docker VM and locked up SSH. Threads default to max(1, ProcessorCount/2).
- Field reports A9/A10: reworded 'original kept in recycle bin' and dry-run preview action text so users stop reading it as 'MediaDash is hoarding files'.
- Field report B1: sidecars now follow the primary file after a successful move.
- Field report B4: subtitles in Subtitles/ or Subs/ subfolders next to media are detected.
- Field report D2: MissingSubtitle now runs before Transcode so subtitles land before an encode that would rename-orphan them.
- NfoScanner no longer flags valid metadata as corrupt on missing per-Actor extensions or trailing text after </movie>.
- OrphanCleanupScanner: unrelated adjacent folders no longer treated as orphans; scanners emitting non-video paths opt out of scoped-delete so stale rows don't sit forever.
- EmbeddedCoverArtScanner: no longer flags every non-trivial AVI as corrupt.
- SmartHealth probe: no longer stuck on 'Checking SMART status...' forever on probe crash; PowerShell reliability-counter fallback no longer silently misses on trailing whitespace in FriendlyName.
- RecycleBin cross-volume move: .mediadash.tmp staging file is cleaned up when a move throws mid-way.
- LibraryMonitor: ReportFileSystemChanged now fires for both source and destination on move so cached ImageInfo drops.

Privacy
- Anonymous community-stats install ID is now month-rotated: SHA-256(salt || Jellyfin SystemId || year-month), never stored on disk. Prior persistent UUID was stronger linkability than APP/GDPR tolerates for 'aggregate community stats'.

Duplicates - new config
- DuplicateAutoFixConfidence (default 0.80): under Automatic mode, only pairs at or above this confidence are auto-queued.
- DuplicateTitleJaccardVeto (default 0.40): kills pairs whose filename title tokens overlap less than this.
- DuplicateRuntimeVetoPct (default 15%): kills pairs whose runtimes differ by more than this.
- New file_hashes cache table and Confidence column on issues (idempotent migration to schema v4).

Still one binary for both Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0.

Full-scanner community stats, on-by-default opt-in, and first-run wizard layout polish. Dashboard's fix-completion popup and redownload banner now survive a plugin reload.

Features
- Community stats now cover every scanner MediaDash ships. 8 new scanners added to the payload, backend schema, and public views (Ungrouped, LargeTrickplay, SubtitleFonts, OrphanedDebris, CorruptNfo, HeavyTranscode, FailedTranscode, EmbeddedCoverArt) alongside the existing 10.
- Community stats default flipped from off to on for new installs. Existing installs are unchanged; their persisted AnalyticsEnabled value wins. The first-run wizard shows the checkbox pre-ticked; untick in Settings -> Safety at any time to opt out.
- Dashboard's LastFixRun (fix-completion popup) and RedownloadWarnings (Overview banner) are now persisted to the plugin DB via a write-through wrapper. Previously both dropped on every plugin reload, so a mid-day restart made the popup or banner vanish. Rehydrated on plugin start.
- README's community-impact table, docs/index.html impact section, and the monthly-stats GitHub Actions workflow now render rows for all 18 scanner types. docs/PRIVACY.md field table extended to match; opt-out language rewritten throughout.
- Docs screenshots (overview, issues, history, settings) regenerated against the current UI with Blender open-movie sample data - no personal filenames or hostnames.

Bug fixes
- First-run wizard "Skip walkthrough" now mints the anonymous install UUID when analytics is enabled. Previously, skipping the wizard left the ID empty and the reporter silently no-op'd, so an on-by-default install that never completed the walkthrough never actually contributed a single row.
- Wizard step 5 (Oversized files): "Skip HDR files" now sits to the right of "Preferred GPU" in a two-column flex row instead of stacked below the description. Both controls align to the same height.
- Wizard step 8 (Language cleanup): the mdChipInput language pickers no longer sit taller than the emby-select controls next to them. Same 46px height rule that already applied on the Settings tab now applies inside the wizard too.
- Wizard step 2 (Libraries): the "Check library access" button now uses the plugin's mdActionBtn class (rounded pill, primary accent, 44px tall) instead of Jellyfin's raw raised-button styling. Matches the rest of the plugin.
- Wizard step 16 (Community stats): intro copy no longer starts with "Off by default -" and now lists every scanner in the "What's sent" panel.

Reclaim totals now match across the plugin, heavy-transcode fixer works on well-encoded sources, SMART shows correctly on unprivileged Linux, and the History tab lets you slice failures by reason.

Features
- History tab's Failed filter now surfaces a "search by reason" dropdown listing the distinct failure reasons in your history with a count each (Permission denied, I/O error, Cross-device link, File no longer exists, etc.). Selecting one narrows the list; switching the top-level chip clears it.
- SMART pill on the Overview drives now shows a specific hint when smartctl fails due to permissions on Linux: setcap 'cap_sys_rawio+ep' $(which smartctl) for native installs, --cap-add=SYS_RAWIO --device=... for Docker.

Bug fixes
- Overview "Reclaimed since install" and History tab's summary + per-library chart now show the same number. History was summing the paginated 500-row window client-side while Overview summed the entire history server-side, causing the mismatch (e.g. 599 GB vs 8.1 GB). New /History/Stats endpoint aggregates over all history server-side; both panels source the total from it.
- Heavy-transcode / failed-transcode fixes no longer refuse to swap when the re-encoded file is slightly larger than the original. Those fix types exist for direct-play compatibility, not disk savings â€” the size gate is now Quality-only, with a 30% hard cap on the transcode types to guard against misconfigured encode settings.
- SMART pills now appear on library drives on Linux. Library-drive detection was using Path.GetPathRoot which always returns "/" on Linux â€” no library drive was ever flagged, so the SMART probe never ran there. Now uses the deepest-matching mount point via FindDriveForPath.
- smartctl exit_status is now honoured. Non-zero exit (permission denied, unsupported device, no SMART support) returns Unknown with the actual smartctl error message, instead of being mis-interpreted as "self-assessment FAILED".

Features

Features
- Trickplay scanner has a configurable minimum-size threshold (Settings â†’ Trickplay space savings). Default 10 MB filters out per-clip trickplay folders that swamp libraries with many short videos; 0 disables the threshold and flags every convertible folder.

Bug fixes
- Overview "Space you could reclaim" panel now shows reclaimable bytes per issue type (with the file count as a muted parenthetical), and the donut is sized by bytes instead of by count so the visual is proportional to actual reclaim. - Progress bar wrap on the masthead now spans the full width of the scan-state line above it (was previously capped at 36em).

Post-1.0 UI polish and a recycle-bin config regression fix.

Bug fixes
- RecycleBin path no longer requires library-adjacency. Users can point the bin at any writable location (e.g. `/mnt/media/.mediadash-recycle` as a sibling of the library for cross-volume-free moves). Only OS-reserved roots (/etc, /bin, /usr, Windows System32, etc.) are refused.
- Errors tab: badge no longer shows a stale count (e.g. "691") after the tab has been cleared. The periodic status poll now delegates to loadErrors() when the user is on the Errors tab, so badge + list update from the same fetch.
- Issues tab: badge is now sourced from the actual issue list length, so "999+" no longer disagrees with the visible cards.
- Overview issue-shortcut cards now show reclaimable space (bytes / MB / GB) as the primary number, with the file count as a subtitle. Types with no space-savings info still show the raw count.
- Progress bar activity text now spans the full width of the scan-state line above it (was capped at 36em).
- Removed the second empty "Subtitles" settings card that appeared post-1.0 (SubtitleFonts controls are already folded into the SubtitleLanguage card).
- "Collapse all" / "Expand all" button on Settings now truthfully reflects what a click will do: it excludes force-collapsed Off-mode tasks from the state check, and hides itself entirely when nothing on the page is togglable.

- Errors tab: badge no longer shows a stale count (e.g. "691") after the tab has been cleared. The periodic status poll now delegates to loadErrors() when the user is on the Errors tab, so badge + list update from the same fetch.
- Issues tab: badge is now sourced from the actual issue list length, so "999+" no longer disagrees with the visible cards.
- Overview issue-shortcut cards now show reclaimable space (bytes / MB / GB) as the primary number, with the file count as a subtitle. Types with no space-savings info still show the raw count.
- Progress bar activity text now spans the full width of the scan-state line above it (was capped at 36em).
- Removed the second empty "Subtitles" settings card that appeared post-1.0 (SubtitleFonts controls are already folded into the SubtitleLanguage card).

- RecycleBin cross-volume moves verify copy size before deleting the source (no more silent data loss on truncated writes).
- MoveToBin folder names carry a per-batch GUID so same-millisecond recycles no longer collide.
- FileBrowser rename / move now return 409 on concurrent-target creation instead of silently overwriting.
- Upload endpoint rejects oversized bodies via Content-Length pre-flight before any disk I/O; 50 GB per-file cap.
- LibraryGuard refuses paths whose ancestor chain contains a symlink or NTFS junction.
- RecycleBinPath must sit inside the plugin data dir or a configured library; OS-reserved roots refused.
- SweepOrphanSidecars enumerates with reparse-point skip and re-checks each candidate before delete.
- IsSimpleName refuses Windows reserved names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9) and trailing dot / space.
- RelocateIssuePaths uses COLLATE NOCASE on the boundary match so sibling issues re-point correctly after case-varying moves on Windows.
- PlayabilityFixer re-verify is reason-driven (audio-kind files no longer recycled on "no-audio" false positives; size-truncated files now actually removed).
- TrackFixer.IsSelfReferentialSubtitle normalises both paths via Path.GetFullPath so legacy relative-path issue rows can't trick the guard.
- MediaSorterFixer cross-volume detection works on Linux (was previously blind because Path.GetPathRoot returns "/").
- MissingSubtitleFixer catches TaskCanceledException from provider network stalls without aborting the whole fix run.
- smartctl / nvidia-smi / df invocations use ArgumentList (no shell tokenization); absolute-path resolution on Linux where possible.
- WMI drive-letter validated before WQL interpolation.
- BulkUpdateOpenIssueStatus chunks at 500 params; controller caps requests at 50 k IDs.
- SmartHealthProbe stdout and stderr drained concurrently before WaitForExit (no more pipe-buffer deadlocks on large SMART payloads).

Bug-fix bundle over 0.9.9.3.

Duplicate detector no longer flags different files with a shared prefix as duplicates. Replaced the trailing-tag whitelist (which kept missing new suffix combos users reported) with file-name-based edition detection: any variation in the filename between two TMDb-matched files yields a different edition key when 'Treat editions as duplicates' is off. Covers 100% of possible suffix combinations. Byte-identical copies with the same filename still group as duplicates. Regression: 'StarWarsCloneWars2003 - Connecting the Dots.mkv' vs 'StarWarsCloneWars2003 - Bridging the Saga.mkv' â€” now stays as two separate entries.

New Overview banner warns when a MediaDash re-encode gets undone by something external (typically Sonarr/Radarr redownloading a "too-small" file whose size dropped below the quality profile minimum, but also fires on manual recycle-bin restores or backup-restore overwrites).

Detection is evidence-based, not guessed: at the end of every scan MediaDash walks the last 30 days of successful non-dry-run history entries, and for each one where the ORIGINAL is still preserved in the recycle bin, compares the file currently at the same path against the recycled original. If the current file is within 10% of the original size â€” i.e. the same rough size we shrank down â€” the shrunk copy has been replaced. Only paths meeting that concrete size-match trigger the warning. False positives are limited to genuine restores, which are also worth surfacing.

The red banner shows the filename, the shrunk-to size, the current size, and the fix date. Dismissable per browser session; reappears on the next scan if the condition still holds.

Two fixes and a reclaim.

VAAPI hardware encodes now pass -rc_mode VBR to hevc_vaapi / h264_vaapi / av1_vaapi. Mesa VAAPI's default rate-control is CQP, which ignores -b:v/-maxrate and picks a QP that routinely produces output LARGER than a modest-bitrate source â€” the "the re-encoded file would be larger than the original, so the original was kept" retry loop that some AMD iGPU users saw every 30-70 minutes on the same file. VBR honours -b:v as the target and -maxrate as the ceiling, so the encoder actually stays under the requested bitrate.

Orphan sidecar sweep: at the end of every fix run (right after the recycle bin purge), MediaDash now walks each library root and deletes any *.mediadash.tmp*, *.mediadash.new*, mediadash.tmp.*, or mediadash.new.* file it finds. These are leftovers from a hard-killed encode (SIGKILL, container restart, Jellyfin crash) where the C# finally block that normally deletes them never ran. Deleted-count + reclaimed-bytes go into Jellyfin's log.

FfmpegExecutor now sweeps for orphaned MediaDash ffmpeg processes before spawning a new encode. Linux only (reads /proc/<pid>/cmdline; Windows/macOS would need extra deps for a very rare failure mode). Any ffmpeg whose command line contains a mediadash.tmp or mediadash.new marker is killed with SIGKILL and its sidecar output file is deleted. Prevents the "two ffmpegs writing to the same output" scenario after a plugin hot-reload or a Jellyfin restart mid-encode. Also cleans up the interleaved-bytes .tmp file that would otherwise sit on disk until the next fix run on the same source overwrote it.

versions.changelog:
- Initial release. - Resolution (isHd/is4K) passthrough for client filtering. - Fix: filtering by a library returned no items. The library (parentId) is now
  resolved into its contents so video range / codec / audio filters work when
  scoped to a specific library.
- Renamed the plugin to "Marquee Companion" (display name only; API route,
  plugin id, and behavior unchanged).
- Capabilities are now scoped to the requested library (parentId): the available
  values offered for a library are drawn only from items in that library, so any
  single facet selection is guaranteed to match at least one item there. Omitting
  parentId still returns the global value set.
- TV libraries now filter correctly by stream facets. Stream attributes live on
  episodes, but TV libraries are browsed at the series level; the filter now
  matches episodes and returns the shows that have at least one matching episode.
  Also forces a recursive query so a library id resolves to its contents.
- Added opt-in recent podcast discovery through Podcast Index. - Podcast discovery now logs why it returned nothing. The endpoint still answers 404 for
  every failure, but the server log distinguishes disabled credentials, a Podcast Index
  rejection, and feeds dropped during validation — including a per-rule tally of what was
  dropped.
- Removes the YouTube trailer resolver. Clients now hand YouTube trailers to the YouTube
  app instead, so the server no longer downloads, verifies, updates, or executes yt-dlp or a
  JavaScript runtime.
- Removes the yt-dlp and JavaScript-runtime downloads earlier versions installed. Those
  binaries are unreachable now the resolver is gone, so the plugin reclaims the directory it
  created rather than leaving an administrator to find it. Only its own install root is
  touched, and a failure to delete never stops the plugin starting.
- Fix: Podcast Discovery always returned 404 when enabled. Podcast Index sends the envelope's
  `status` as a JSON boolean, but it was bound to a string, so the whole recent-feeds payload
  failed to deserialize. Both the boolean and the documented string form are now accepted, and
  an unusable payload is logged with the value exactly as it arrived.
- Added opt-in email sign-in. A client posts an email address, the server mails a single-use
  link, and confirming that link signs the waiting device in — no password, and no typing on a
  TV remote. The email can be opened on any device, so it works for tvOS; when it is opened on
  the signing-in device itself, the confirmation page also offers a deep link straight back into
  the app. Unrecognised addresses can optionally register, in which case the new account is
  created disabled and copies an administrator-chosen template user's permissions, so nothing is

  only 247 had an AC-3 track that was itself 5.1 — the rest were "DTS 5.1 main track plus
  AC-3 2.0 commentary" files that answered "has AC-3" and "has six channels" separately.
  Codec, channel count and spatial format are now read per audio track and have to hold on
  ONE of them. A filter naming a single audio facet is unaffected. The values offered by
  /Capabilities are unchanged.
- Music libraries can now be filtered by codec and channel count. Tracks were never
  catalogued, so every audio filter over a music library returned nothing at all while the
  same library unfiltered returned 11,022 tracks.
- Release-date recovery reads the FILE NAME first and falls back to date added, and
  understands two-digit-year release names (Name.25.02.05.Title). Date added is when a
  file reached the server, not when it was released: on a 650-item dry run, leading with
  it produced 18 distinct dates with 605 identical, while the name gave 98 spanning 2013
  to 2026.
- Release-date recovery is chosen PER LIBRARY. - Added opt-in release-date recovery. Downloaded YouTube content carries its upload
  date only in the file name, so Jellyfin stores no premiere date and reads the leading
  YYYYMMDD as a production year like 20250823 — those items then cannot appear in any
  view ordered by release date, on any client. A new scheduled task, "Recover missing
  release dates", reads the date from the production-year stamp, an sYYYY.eMMDDnn name,
  or a bare YYYYMMDD run, and writes it along with the corrected year. Off by default,
  previews to the log until an administrator turns preview off, and never modifies an
  item that already has a release date.
- Adds the seamless Marquee Companion panel to Jellyfin Web without manual web-client changes. - Adds paired Jellyfin 10/.NET 9 and Jellyfin 12/.NET 10 package builds.

- Initial release. - Resolution (isHd/is4K) passthrough for client filtering. - Fix: filtering by a library returned no items. The library (parentId) is now
  resolved into its contents so video range / codec / audio filters work when
  scoped to a specific library.
- Renamed the plugin to "Marquee Companion" (display name only; API route,
  plugin id, and behavior unchanged).
- Capabilities are now scoped to the requested library (parentId): the available
  values offered for a library are drawn only from items in that library, so any
  single facet selection is guaranteed to match at least one item there. Omitting
  parentId still returns the global value set.
- TV libraries now filter correctly by stream facets. Stream attributes live on
  episodes, but TV libraries are browsed at the series level; the filter now
  matches episodes and returns the shows that have at least one matching episode.
  Also forces a recursive query so a library id resolves to its contents.
- Added opt-in recent podcast discovery through Podcast Index. - Podcast discovery now logs why it returned nothing. The endpoint still answers 404 for
  every failure, but the server log distinguishes disabled credentials, a Podcast Index
  rejection, and feeds dropped during validation — including a per-rule tally of what was
  dropped.
- Removes the YouTube trailer resolver. Clients now hand YouTube trailers to the YouTube
  app instead, so the server no longer downloads, verifies, updates, or executes yt-dlp or a
  JavaScript runtime.
- Removes the yt-dlp and JavaScript-runtime downloads earlier versions installed. Those
  binaries are unreachable now the resolver is gone, so the plugin reclaims the directory it
  created rather than leaving an administrator to find it. Only its own install root is
  touched, and a failure to delete never stops the plugin starting.
- Fix: Podcast Discovery always returned 404 when enabled. Podcast Index sends the envelope's
  `status` as a JSON boolean, but it was bound to a string, so the whole recent-feeds payload
  failed to deserialize. Both the boolean and the documented string form are now accepted, and
  an unusable payload is logged with the value exactly as it arrived.
- Added opt-in email sign-in. A client posts an email address, the server mails a single-use
  link, and confirming that link signs the waiting device in — no password, and no typing on a
  TV remote. The email can be opened on any device, so it works for tvOS; when it is opened on
  the signing-in device itself, the confirmation page also offers a deep link straight back into
  the app. Unrecognised addresses can optionally register, in which case the new account is
  created disabled and copies an administrator-chosen template user's permissions, so nothing is
  accessible until an administrator enables it. SMTP host, port, security, credentials and
  from-address are configured in the plugin settings, along with link lifetime and rate limits;
  a "send test email" button reports the mail server's own error when submission fails. The
  endpoint reports an explicit error rather than a silent success when SMTP is not configured.

versions.changelog:
## v1.7.1.0
### New
- Redesigned settings page.
- New "Remove plain lyrics that hide synced lyrics" option, on by default. Turn it off if other apps use the lyrics files in your music folder.
### Fixes
- Synced lyrics now show up even when a plain .txt sits next to the song. Before, Jellyfin kept showing the plain lyrics and the task re-downloaded the synced ones every run. -> #59

## v1.7.1.0
### New
- Redesigned settings page.
- New "Remove plain lyrics that hide synced lyrics" option, on by default. Turn it off if other apps use the lyrics files in your music folder.
### Fixes
- Synced lyrics now show up even when a plain .txt sits next to the song. Before, Jellyfin kept showing the plain lyrics and the task re-downloaded the synced ones every run. -> #59

## v1.7.0.0
### New
- Jellyfin 12 support. Every release now ships two builds, one for Jellyfin 12 and one for Jellyfin 10.11, and Jellyfin installs the right one for your server automatically.
- Jellyfin 10.11.0 and newer are supported again. The previous release required at least 10.11.6.
- New "Disable rate limiting" option for self-hosted LRCLIB servers. It removes the delay between requests, which speeds up large libraries. Requests to the public lrclib.net stay rate limited.
### Fixes
- Tracks that only have an album artist tag (compilations, classical music, many rips) now get lyrics. Strict search used to give up without an artist tag, and fuzzy search ignored the album artist entirely.
- Fuzzy search now tries every artist tagged on a track instead of only the first one.
- A system clock jump (NTP correction, VM resume) can no longer stall lyric requests.

## v1.7.0.0
### New
- Jellyfin 12 support. Every release now ships two builds, one for Jellyfin 12 and one for Jellyfin 10.11, and Jellyfin installs the right one for your server automatically.
- Jellyfin 10.11.0 and newer are supported again. The previous release required at least 10.11.6.
- New "Disable rate limiting" option for self-hosted LRCLIB servers. It removes the delay between requests, which speeds up large libraries. Requests to the public lrclib.net stay rate limited.
### Fixes
- Tracks that only have an album artist tag (compilations, classical music, many rips) now get lyrics. Strict search used to give up without an artist tag, and fuzzy search ignored the album artist entirely.
- Fuzzy search now tries every artist tagged on a track instead of only the first one.
- A system clock jump (NTP correction, VM resume) can no longer stall lyric requests.

## v1.6.6.0
### Fixes
- The lyrics task no longer re-downloads tracks that already have synced lyrics on disk. When a track's lyrics were saved but the database still reported them as plain (Jellyfin doesn't refresh metadata after a download until the next library scan), the task kept "upgrading" the same tracks on every run. It now trusts the synced .lrc file already on disk and skips it. -> #43

## v1.6.5.0
### Fixes
- Build against Jellyfin 10.11.6 instead of always the latest release. Previous builds were linked against 10.11.10 assemblies, which made Jellyfin report the plugin as "not supported" (TypeLoadException) on older 10.11.x servers. The plugin is now compatible with Jellyfin 10.11.6 and newer. -> #55

## v1.6.4.0
### Fixes
- Lyric file detection now also checks Jellyfin's internal metadata folder, not just the media folder. With "Save lyrics into media folders" disabled, already-downloaded lyrics are detected instead of being re-downloaded on every task run, which also reduces load on lrclib.net -> #54

## v1.6.3.0
### What's New
- Optional self-hosted LRCLIB server URL: point the plugin at your own LRCLIB instance instead of lrclib.net. Subpath URLs are preserved and the URL is validated on save. Thanks to @Nausi-llon (#50).
- Built-in rate limiting for lrclib.net requests: enforces a 200 ms minimum gap between calls and honors HTTP 429 `Retry-After` so transient spikes back off cleanly instead of surfacing as per-track errors.
- Identifiable User-Agent on every lrclib request (`jellyfin-plugin-lyrics/<version> (+repo-url)`) so the LRCLIB operators can distinguish this plugin from `jellyfin/jellyfin-plugin-lrclib` (#49).

### Notes
- No configuration changes required for existing users — the self-host URL defaults to `https://lrclib.net` and the rate limit only kicks in under load.

## v1.6.2.0
### What's New
- Auto-removes the official "LrcLib Lyrics" plugin (`jellyfin-plugin-lrclib`) on startup if installed, since both plugins register the same lyrics provider and conflict. This plugin is a fork that fixes critical issues — see README. The old plugin can be reinstalled later to switch back.

## v1.6.1.0
### What's New
- Lyrics alternative discovery: skip re-downloading lyrics that already failed in a previous run
- Synced-lyric upgrade now checks the existing sidecar file before replacing plain text

### Fixes
- Stop matching instrumental tracks against unrelated songs: honor LRCLIB's instrumental flag, validate every match against requested duration and artist, and drop the track-name-only fuzzy fallback when artist info is available (#40)
- Scheduled task log: split DB-desync skips from "already synced" skips so plain `.txt` sidecars are no longer counted as synced

### Settings
- New configurable duration-tolerance filter (default on, ±15s) with UI toggle to tune or disable

### Notes
- Jellyfin 10.11.6 or newer is now recommended (see README)

## v1.6.0.0
### What's New
- Added song title cleanup to strip YouTube-style suffixes (Official Music Video, etc.) and duplicate artist names
- Added progressive search fallback: retries with fewer parameters when no results are found
- Added multi-artist support: splits "artist1/artist2" and tries each artist individually
- Replace non-synced lyrics with synced ones when available
- Sped up scheduled lyrics task

### Fixes
- Fixed DI issue with RetryStateStore causing plugin to malfunction on startup
- Fixed fuzzy search failing when album name is missing
- Fixed crash on missing artist or invalid id

### Defaults Changed
- Strict search is now disabled by default
- "Exclude album name" is now enabled by default

## v1.5.0.0
### What's New
- Fixed support for Jellyfin 10.11

## v1.4.0.0
### What's New
- Added support for Jellyfin 10.11

## v1.3.0.0
### What's New
- Fixed a lot of plugin loading issues
- Fixed GitHub Action Workflows

### Technical Improvements
- Consistent versioning across all project files
- Better package compatibility with Jellyfin 10.9.x series
- Improved documentation and installation instructions

name: SponsorBlock [✓]
description:
Skip sponsored segments in YouTube videos using SponsorBlock data.  
  
Universal Repo:  
Generated: 03:08 UTC  
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/felixfoertsch/jellyfin-sponsorblock/main/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/felixfoertsch/jellyfin-sponsorblock

versions.changelog: Add an opt-in Jellyfin metadata source for YouTube IDs. Preserve filename and custom-regex matching as the default, read validated Youtube provider IDs imported from NFO uniqueid metadata, and expose the source choice in plugin settings.

Add Jellyfin 12 support. Retarget to .NET 10 and Jellyfin Controller 12.0.0-rc3, implement the new media-segment cleanup contract, and preserve the event-driven SponsorBlock workflow without enabling the core library segment scan.
Serialize SponsorBlock processing to avoid concurrent refresh and playback work for the same item. Bump the plugin version for local installation.

Add Done state with convergence-based polling. Videos older than 30 days (by YouTube publish date) are fetched once and frozen. Videos younger than 30 days are polled daily until segment data is unchanged for 5 consecutive checks, then frozen. Stale segments are now deleted when SponsorBlock data disappears. Daily scan task refactored to a clean two-phase dispatcher.

Add dedicated SponsorBlock log file (log_SponsorBlock_YYYYMMDD.log) in Jellyfin's log directory. All info/warning/error events now write to both the main server log and the dedicated file, so the plugin appears as a separate log entry in the Jellyfin dashboard.

Add comprehensive logging to the orchestrator and triggers. Every decision point (scope check, path empty, ID extraction failure, state-machine skip, segment write, state transition) now logs at information or debug level, so issues are diagnosable directly from the Jellyfin log dashboard.
Fix EnumerateScoped to discover Episode and Movie items, not just standalone Video. YouTube libraries imported as TV Shows store items as Episode type, which BaseItemKind.Video did not match.

Fix automatic loading for old archives and restore DLL-only release packaging. The daily refresh now discovers selected-library videos older than the sanity-check window, old untracked items use their Jellyfin DateCreated for the 48-hour decision, and NoData rows recheck after cooldown instead of being terminal.

Add a one-shot Force Scan button for existing archives. Admins can backfill every video in the selected libraries once, while the normal daily refresh stays limited to tracked Pending and HasData items. Includes duplicate-scan protection and status endpoints.

Repair pruned SponsorBlock segments on playback. When Jellyfin refreshes a changed media file it can delete generated MediaSegment rows while the plugin state still says HasData; playback start now verifies that Jellyfin still has segment rows and re-fetches/recreates them if they were pruned.

Fix delayed SponsorBlock loading. Register the daily refresh scheduled task so Pending items are retried automatically, correct the 24-hour playback retry condition, and wait for playback-start processing so freshly fetched segments can reach the first playback session.

Actually fix segments not reaching clients. Jellyfin's IMediaSegmentManager.CreateSegmentAsync expects the second arg to be the MD5-derived provider id (new Guid(MD5(name.ToLowerInvariant() UTF-16 LE)).ToString("N")), not the literal provider name. We were passing "SponsorBlock" verbatim, so stored segments didn't match any registered provider and the public MediaSegments API filtered them out. Pre-compute the hash and pass that. After upgrading, hit Reset on the config page so old segments get re-fetched under the correct provider id.

Fix segments not reaching clients. v1.1.0.0 dropped the IMediaSegmentProvider registration to avoid the slow scan, but Jellyfin filters segments by registered provider, so stored segments were never served. Re-register a stub provider (Supports => false, GetMediaSegments => empty) so Jellyfin recognizes 'SponsorBlock' as a known provider while the orchestrator stays in charge of fetching.

Add admin Reset button on the plugin config page that wipes SponsorBlock state and owned segments for items in the configured library scope, so the orchestrator re-fetches on next playback. Useful for re-fetching items whose SponsorBlock data became available after the initial scan.

Replace media-segment scan with event-driven orchestrator. Add daily refresh task at configurable hour. Add per-library scoping (empty by default — admin must opt in). SQLite per-item state machine (Pending/HasData/NoData) with 48h sanity check.
Remove non-functional user segment actions table from config page.
Initial release.

versions.changelog: For Jellyfin 12. Jellyfin's own search now also finds titles by meaning, shown in the usual Movies, Shows and Episodes rows after the title matches. New options: turn it on or off, only use it for searches that look like a sentence, limit how many matches it adds, hide the AI search button completely (native search only), and keep a log of every search for a few days so an admin or API key can collect them.
Fixes the search button missing on new Docker installs.

One unified setup: a chat endpoint plus a local or remote retrieval source (replaces the old Direct/Platform modes). New: search without a language model, returning retrieval matches ranked by relevance with no per-result reasons. Embedding model is now a dropdown, and endpoints are configured per capability.
Show more now returns new titles instead of repeating the first results. Recommendations no longer come back empty on reasoning models.
Fixed a bug when choosing TV or Movies in platform mode.

versions.changelog: Corretto il doppio caricamento dopo un aggiornamento (issue #2): lo ZIP contiene un meta.json con il nome del plugin, così Jellyfin tiene tutte le versioni sotto lo stesso nome e rimuove la vecchia, e all'avvio il plugin segna come superate le proprie copie più vecchie. Licenza AGPLv3 con termini aggiuntivi (attribuzione, versioni modificate riconoscibili, marchi e mascotte); attribuzione e link al codice sorgente nella pagina del plugin. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AniList come fonte senza chiave insieme a TMDB: cast giapponese con i personaggi, studio di animazione, date, stato, voto, trailer, copertina e banner, solo nei campi vuoti. L'anno di una stagione senza date arriva dalla catena dei sequel di AniList, se gli episodi coincidono. Gli ID AniList che non corrispondono per tipo o anno vengono ignorati. Nuovo passo AniList nel setup. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Comunità per tutti: dopo una correzione il plugin chiede se condividerla e la invia tramite il servizio della comunità, senza account; il token GitHub diventa facoltativo. Si condividono anche le stagioni con una scheda propria, applicate agli altri solo se numero di stagione ed episodi coincidono. Elenco approvato aggiornato ogni giorno, controlli automatici e approvazione con un'etichetta, tessera Comunità in Inizio, passo Comunità nel setup e scelta della stagione in «Correggi un abbinamento». Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Pagina del plugin rifatta da zero con l'identità di AnimeClick: setup guidato al primo avvio e solo i passi nuovi dopo gli aggiornamenti importanti, vetrina degli ultimi anime aggiornati, cruscotto della collezione, libreria a locandine con titoli e trame uniti per anime, attivazione delle librerie a un clic e ricerca della scheda su AnimeClick per correggere un abbinamento. Corretti i conteggi dell'analisi di una singola serie, lo stato della condivisione comunitaria appena attivata e «Da verificare», che ora coincide con quanto «Sistema tutti i titoli» ricontrolla. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Scarta i titoli alternativi di un'altra stagione verificando il titolo inglese originale. Quando manca una fonte coerente, traduce il titolo inglese già valido; esclude i nomi dei file. Correzione trovata sul NAS in anteprima, senza salvare la proposta errata. Include le novità 1.2.1. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AnimeClick come unico provider remoto per le librerie anime: identificazione TMDB verificata, completamento dei metadati senza altri plugin e immagini integrate Fanart → TMDB → AnimeClick. Chiavi Fanart personale e di progetto nelle impostazioni, con link e verifica. Numerazione, campi bloccati e immagini esistenti conservati. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AnimeClick primo campo per campo: i valori generici lasciano spazio alle fonti configurate. Recupero italiano e traduzione dall’inglese anche per serie, film, generi e tag, senza mescolare titolo e trama. Le immagini conservano la precedenza dei provider ad alta risoluzione; nessun aggiornamento immagini o riparazione viene avviato dall’installazione. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Titoli episodio mancanti: ricerca su TheTVDB e TMDB configurati dopo AnimeClick, precedenza all’italiano e traduzione dei soli titoli inglesi con il profilo AI esistente. Verifica degli ID esterni, conservazione dei titoli compilati e indicazione della fonte nell’avanzamento. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

La tua libreria con analisi automatica, viste separate, avanzamento reale e interruzione dei lavori. Recupero dei soli titoli mancanti con protezione dei metadati esistenti. Abbinamenti della comunità e invio automatico delle correzioni su GitHub, entrambi facoltativi e disattivati di default. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Major per Jellyfin 12 e .NET 10, verificata su 12.0 e 12.1. Interfaccia riprogettata con guida iniziale, preferenze semplici e strumenti avanzati separati. Identificazione automatica più prudente fra titoli simili, remake e stagioni; correzione manuale cercando il titolo in libreria e incollando il link AnimeClick, senza cancellazione diretta delle immagini. Corretti redirect di rete, collisioni e scadenza della cache, concorrenza nei refresh, rate limit e coerenza della coda traduzioni. AI opzionale e disattivabile senza perdere il profilo; impostazioni e credenziali esistenti conservate. 210 test backend per versione server e 11 test browser. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo: non installare su 10.11; le release precedenti restano disponibili. Dettagli e limiti delle verifiche nel rapporto di audit della release.

name: Mind the Gaps [✓]
description:
Scans your library for gaps (missing movies in partially-owned collections and franchises, missing series content, unowned titles from actor and director filmographies, and related recommendations) using TMDB, Trakt, TheTVDB, and TVmaze, with music and book sources (MusicBrainz, OpenLibrary, Discogs), and reads the watchlists and want-lists you already keep on those sites. Presents an easy todo list for filling out your collection, diagnoses why a title is reported missing, surfaces where to watch each item, and can optionally mint native virtual placeholders for missing items.

versions.changelog: 10.11.11.0 - Want to watch gains three options, all off by default and all requiring the arrived-titles playlist (contributed by David Rappo, @rappo, in PR 21): the home row can lead with the titles already on your playlist, a title comes off the playlist once it is watched (a series once every episode is played), and a movie or series page gets a bookmark button among its own. Plugin rows are reachable with a TV remote's D-pad. Not interested, off by default, lets each user hide a title from their own Web UI pages without hiding it for anyone else. A user with a parental rating limit sees the Web UI sections narrowed to the titles that limit allows, rather than none of them. The home Discover row, the Want to watch row, and the item page rows each have a placement setting; existing settings carry over. The Gaps Report's toolbar is grouped by what each control acts on, every header has a select-all, a line above the list says how many rows the filters hide, and Add to TODO is now Add to watchlist. The report is usable at phone width, and the settings page has collapsible sections, a search, and better screen reader support. A new scheduled task, Prune gaps from deleted items, takes deleted library items out of the report: a gap they were the only source of is removed, and one with other sources moves to the next. It has no default schedule; it waits for a running scan, and a second scan waits for the first. Recommendation groups link to the owned title they came from. Books get an OpenLibrary id field and albums and artists a Discogs id field in the metadata editor, with a link on the item's page; a dedicated OpenLibrary or Discogs plugin takes over when installed. Links are built from each title's ids when the report loads, so a link plugin installed later applies everywhere. The report takes far less memory and disk (on a library with 83,000 gaps, about 1.6 GB down to 200 MB in memory and 245 MB down to 131 MB on disk), loads in about half the time, and is written far less often during scans and where-to-watch lookups. Existing reports convert on first load; a report saved by this version cannot be read by an earlier one, so going back shows an empty report until its next scan.

Mark fetched closes the title for every requester in one action, and Verify all checks the queue against the library and closes a title you already have, however it arrived. Send to the acquisition stack is done from the Gaps Report. An administrator can manage another user's want-to-watch list. versions.changelog:
### Added

- A Quality column that names the class a frame falls in, from 144p to 8K, with an i in place of the p for interlaced video. It sorts by class rather than by how the name reads, and a filter picks a class from a list and holds rows at, above or below it. (#7)
- `Schema` answers the classes a quality can be held against, in their order.
- A failed export and a failed column save are reported in words of their own.

### Changed

- A CSV names the unit of a size, a runtime and a bitrate in its header. An ODS shows a runtime as a time, counted in hours past a day, and a size and a bitrate with their unit, all of them still numbers a spreadsheet can total. (#6)
- A number typed into a filter with the digit grouping the table prints is read as one number, so 48,000 is no longer 48.
- The README describes `search` and what an export holds, and names bytes per hour and truth values among the filter values.
- An advisory against a package Jellyfin brings along is a build warning rather than an error.

### Fixed

- The sidebar entry followed a language further down the browser's list when English came first, and could take one the browser had ruled out.
- A book ran for the second Jellyfin measures its reading progress in, and was given a size per hour from it.
- A series whose episodes run at 24000/1001 and at 2997/125 read as mixed in its frame rate, though every episode shows 23.976.
- A DVD or Blu-ray folder weighed only the first file of its title. It now weighs every file in the folder and shows no size per hour.
- A .strm took its bitrate and its size per hour from the bytes of the text file.
- The table kept its scroll position when a page turn, a sort, a search or a filter replaced its rows.
- A visit whose schema failed to load left an empty page behind, and a later one left the filter button disabled.
- Two quick changes to the rows per page or to the level a tab is expanded to could be stored in the wrong order.
- The spacing of the tab counts, the column picker and the row toggles did not follow a right-to-left layout.
- Three checks could not fail or skipped part of what they name: the rounded runtime of a series, the version in the README badge, and the names of the tabs.
- A failed library refresh ended the test run, a request the server never answered held it for good, and Ctrl-C waited for the helper container to finish.
- The fixture recipe of the screenshot script went on after a failed encode, and the version list did not retry a connection that dropped after the request was sent.

### Dependencies

- jsdom 30.1.1 in the tests. (#4)
- Renovate keeps `test/` in its scan through an empty `ignorePaths` rather than `ignorePresets`.

### Added

- Conditions on any column, up to twenty per request: at least, at most, equals, differs from, contains, does not contain, is empty and is not empty, whichever of them fit the column. A value is typed in the unit the table shows, a filtered tab lists the level it is expanded to, flat, and an export writes exactly those rows.
- Inventory has its own entry in the dashboard sidebar, worded in the language the browser asks in.
- The table opens on the Inventory logo, worded in the language the page is in and linking to the project.
- Music filed loose beside the albums is listed with them, since no row opens to reach it.
- The plugin archive carries its image, so the catalog and the plugins page show the logo rather than an empty tile.
- `Schema` answers the conditions each column can be held against and how many of them one request may carry.

### Changed

- The Music tab counts tracks rather than albums, and is called Music rather than Albums.
- The table fills the window, with its header held in place while the rows scroll.
- Plays and Plays (all users) read 0 rather than an empty cell, so a condition and a sort can hold them.
- Size, duration and bitrate are held against a range rather than an exact value, which a column shown rounded to a unit could never meet.
- A number is typed with a decimal comma where the language uses one, and a value that cannot be read is marked rather than quietly dropped.
- Leaving the page and coming back finds the tab the way it was left, with its sort and its page.
- Every text cell of a CSV is quoted once it holds a separator, whichever one the file itself uses.
- A film or episode kept in several cuts, any of them split into parts, reports the bytes of every file. It and the folders above it show no size per hour, and its bitrate is that of the cut being served.
- A manual install is described by the plugins folder of the server's data directory, rather than by the Docker path alone.
- Bug reports ask for the steps, a screenshot and the log lines; a pull request agrees to the contributor license agreement by checkbox, which a workflow checks.

### Fixed

- A filtered table of fewer than five rows collapsed to nothing on a low window.
- A film grouped with a version in another library was weighed twice on Jellyfin 12.1.
- A film played in its second cut showed no play count and no date, though Jellyfin counts it played.
- Firefox showed rows above the table header after a wheel scroll.
- A second address for the page bound its controls to the view the web client had kept, leaving the new one empty.
- A page turned inside the pause after typing a condition left the table behind the end of what it lists.
- A page left behind by a library that shrank falls back to the last page there is.
- A condition on a column a plugin update no longer offers took the whole page down, on that visit and every later one.
- The page stops offering conditions once the server would refuse another.
- Exports in Arabic and Persian wrote a decimal separator no spreadsheet reads.
- A download the browser gave up on is no longer logged as a server error.
- A failed request no longer leaves another tab's rows on screen or skips the page, sort and total that are drawn, and the column picker no longer stores a selection for a level that is not shown.
- An expanded row closes again when the table it was opened in is replaced, and expansion requests left over from another tab are no longer sent.
- A numeric first column is no longer right-aligned where rows expand, which hid their indentation, and height is printed without digit grouping.
- The API rejects `parentIds` as soon as one id is not a guid.
- The first build of a table asks which library a folder belongs to once rather than once per item in it.

### Security

- A name holding a semicolon or a tab could start a formula in a spreadsheet set to split there, since only the separator of the file itself was quoted.
- An invented culture name on an export answered with an error and grew a cache that is never freed, and a lone surrogate in a condition answered with an error as well. Both are refused now.
- A configuration saved through Jellyfin's own endpoint with empty lists made every endpoint of the plugin fail until the next restart.

### Dependencies

- Renovate follows the Node, jsdom and Playwright versions the tests are pinned to, alongside the GitHub Actions and the analyzers it already tracked.

### Added

- Rows per page, chosen in the footer and kept across restarts, from 50 up to 10000.
- Three columns totalling playback over every account on the server: how often something was played, when it last was, and how many accounts have played it to the end, which on a folder counts only the accounts that have played everything below it.
- The tab whose rows are on their way and the export being built now show that they are working.
- `Schema` reports the culture it answered in, which is what the page takes its plural form from.

### Changed

- What was labelled Played is now Fully played, since Jellyfin only ticks it when something ran to the end.
- The export is written to a temporary file rather than built in memory, and stops when the browser goes away.
- `Items` and `Export` refuse a sort column they do not know instead of quietly sorting by the first one.
- Every change is tested against each Jellyfin release from 12.0 on, one run per major and minor version, taken from the published image tags.

### Fixed

- A film split across several files reported the size of the first file alone, and no runtime at all.
- A trailer or a making of sitting beside a film was listed as an item of its own, in a tab of its own, and its bytes counted towards the totals.
- The frame rate could read 1000 fps where Jellyfin's own interface shows the real one.
- An item Jellyfin marks played on reaching the end of playback did not reach the table until the next stop report.
- The two dropdowns had no arrow, the search field put an empty label into the toolbar, and a disabled button looked exactly like one that could be clicked.
- A first load that failed left the page blank, with an empty column picker behind the Columns button.
- Expanding a level asked for every fifty rows at once, so a large page could open hundreds of requests at a time.
- A row that turned out to have nothing below it lost its control, its alignment with the rows around it, and the keyboard focus.
- A long path was never shortened, and the footer could not wrap in a narrow window.
- The page indicator is announced when it changes, and the control that opens a row says which row it opens.

### Dependencies

- The release archive is uploaded with the gh CLI; softprops/action-gh-release is no longer used.

### Added

- One table in the dashboard listing everything in the libraries, from a whole series down to a single episode, with 38 columns across General, Video, Audio, Subtitles and Playback.
- Folder rows total what is below them: size, runtime and item count add up, an attribute the children disagree on reads as Mixed, and playback folds from the episodes or tracks underneath.
- A column selection per level and how far a tab opens, both remembered across restarts.
- Search across every level of a tab, sorting on any column, and paging.
- Export of the current view as CSV or ODS, in the language of the interface.
- English, German, Spanish, French and Italian.

versions.changelog: # 🚀 A New Foundation for File Transformation File Transformation **3.0.0.0** is a major overhaul of how the plugin integrates with Jellyfin. The transformation system has been rebuilt around standard ASP.NET Core middleware, removing much of the version-specific runtime patching that File Transformation previously relied on. Alongside **Jellyfin 12 support**, this release drops support for **Jellyfin 10.10.7** and lays a much more maintainable foundation for future Jellyfin releases. > ## 🙌 Huge thanks to @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv > > A massive part of this release is thanks to **@4eh5xitv6787h645ebv**, who took on the major overhaul of File Transformation's core architecture in PR #58. > > The move away from the old Harmony/MonoMod-based interception system to standard ASP.NET Core middleware is a significant piece of work. It not only makes File Transformation substantially easier to maintain, but also resolves an entire class of compatibility problems that caused the plugin to malfunction or be disabled on certain Jellyfin versions and platforms (#20, #35, #62, #64, #70, #71). > > This is far more than a small patch or isolated feature - it fundamentally improves the foundation the plugin is built on. A huge thank you for the time and effort that went into it. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and the newer Jellyfin server architecture (#34). * Replaced the previous Harmony/MonoMod-based web interception system with standard ASP.NET Core `IStartupFilter` middleware (PR #58, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv). * Added support for unregistering transformations through `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing dependent plugins to cleanly remove transformations when required. * Added support for synthesising virtual files for registered transformation paths, restoring support for plugins such as Plugin Pages where the underlying file doesn't physically exist. * Added ETag generation and `304 Not Modified` support for transformed content. * Added Brotli and gzip recompression of transformed responses for remote clients. * Added automatic MIME type detection for virtual transformed files. ## 🛠️ Improvements * Removed platform-specific DLL extraction and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * Removed dependencies on Harmony, MonoMod and Prometheus from the core transformation pipeline. * Improved compatibility across Jellyfin versions and platforms by moving the transformation system onto standard ASP.NET Core APIs (#20, #35, #62, #64). * Added per-transformation error isolation so a failure in one plugin's transformation won't prevent other transformations from running. * Made transformation registration, removal and execution thread-safe. * Added regex caching and timeout protection for transformation matching. * Improved handling of `Accept-Encoding`, including proper quality-value (`q`) parsing. * Improved LAN detection for IPv6-mapped IPv4 addresses. * Improved proxy caching behaviour by correctly setting `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. * Reworked HTTP handling to use a shared `HttpClient` with appropriate timeouts. * Hardened named-pipe transformations with timeouts, size limits, EOF handling and improved resource cleanup. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed a class of failures where Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching could cause File Transformation to malfunction or be automatically disabled on startup (#20, #35, #62, #64, #71). * Fixed #70 where transformations could attempt to use a disposed `IServiceProvider` after Jellyfin restarted, resulting in `500` responses across the web UI. * Fixed transformed content potentially retaining stale trailing bytes when a transformation produced a shorter result than the original response. * Fixed failures in one transformation potentially breaking the entire transformation pipeline. * Fixed potential `HttpClient` resource leaks. * Fixed named-pipe transformations being able to hang indefinitely or loop on zero-byte reads. * Fixed incorrect handling of disabled compression encodings such as `gzip;q=0`. * Fixed failed virtual-file transformations returning an empty successful response instead of reverting to the original `404`. * Improved middleware failure handling so the original response is served if transformation or recompression fails. ## 💻 Developer Compatibility The existing `PluginInterface.RegisterTransformation` API and registration payload remain compatible with previous releases, so plugins using a standard transformation callback **should not need to change how they register transformations**. There are, however, some changes to transformation execution that plugin developers should be aware of: * Added `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing plugins to explicitly unregister a previously registered transformation. * Assembly callbacks still receive the same payload and are expected to return the transformed content as a `string`. * Invalid or failed assembly callbacks now **fail safely rather than falling through to another configured callback mechanism**. Plugins should ensure their callback assembly, class and method names are valid. * HTTP transformation callbacks must now return a **successful HTTP status code**. Non-success responses are treated as a failed transformation rather than using the response body as transformed content. * HTTP callbacks now have a **15 second timeout**. * Named-pipe callbacks now have connection/error handling and a **50 MB maximum response size**. * Failed transformations now leave the original response untouched rather than potentially replacing it with invalid or partial output. These changes are intended to make transformations significantly safer and more predictable, but plugins relying on the previous fallback or error behaviour should review their integrations when updating. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and its newer server architecture (#34). * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier File Transformation release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Removed legacy Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * File Transformation now relies on standard ASP.NET Core middleware rather than patching Jellyfin internals, providing a much more stable base for future Jellyfin versions. ## Contributors * 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). versions.changelog:
v3.0.0.4 - Per-library file counts, boxset link fix

- The Per-Library Breakdown now shows a file count below every size value (trickplay folders included), so sparse and dense libraries are distinguishable at a glance
- Boxset library rows no longer link into the Library Explorer, whose scope excludes boxsets; they render as plain text instead of opening an empty state
- Every task dropdown in Settings now explains what the task does, via an info button next to each task name, in all dashboard languages
- The Overview Trickplay card now also shows the space used by trickplay images Jellyfin stores internally, on its own line below the alongside-media total, marked with an (internal) badge, or as the headline when no alongside data exists
- Compact log view on phones: log entries stack as cards below 700 px instead of squeezing into a four-column table, so no horizontal scrolling is needed, and rows keep breathing room at the screen edges
- Roomier Library Explorer filter popovers on phones using nearly the full viewport width, like the bitrate editor
- Tested by 6219 unit tests and 352 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.1 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.3 - Library Explorer, new Codecs breakdowns, disabled users ignored

- The Codecs tab now has a Library Explorer: combine resolution, codecs, bitrate, languages, watched users and formats into one search, scoped to the libraries you pick in its multi-select, so you can find e.g. all 4K films with low bitrate
- Options with zero matches under the other filters are hidden automatically, dimensions without matches stay greyed out, and multi-value dropdowns accept several audio languages, subtitle languages or users at once
- Every active filter is shown in the result header and a Reset button clears the whole search; results arrive as the familiar grouped file tree with Movies, TV Shows and other sections
- Jump straight into the search from the Overview: each library name and all four media cards open the Explorer pre-filtered to that scope
- Every categorical filter can be negated with Includes/Excludes, so you can search e.g. audio languages that are not German; excluded picks show as ≠ pills and counts preview what stays
- Four new breakdowns in the Codecs tab, each with drill-down to the exact files: Video Bitrate (7 tiers from < 2 to > 60 Mbps), Audio Languages, Subtitle Languages and Watched (by username plus Never watched)
- Each bitrate tier uses what Jellyfin measured for the video stream; when a file has no per-stream value the average is estimated from its size and runtime, so almost every file lands in a real tier instead of Unknown
- Disabled Jellyfin users no longer skew results: their old plays are excluded from Smart Recommendations, watch history and the new Watched breakdown
- Long breakdowns start collapsed behind a Show-all toggle with Unknown always last, and unreadable language tags fold into Unknown instead of junk entries
- Added responsive, independently scrollable library result cards.
- Improved compact layouts for mobile controls.
- Added consistent themed scrollbar styling across plugin panels and lists.
- The Overview Per-Library Breakdown has a new Other column per library covering NFO files, text files and other unrecognized sidecar files, plus a Books column whenever a book library exists, so every row adds up exactly to its Total
- Tested by 6169 unit tests and 341 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.1 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.2 - Log tab, save bar, resolution and touch fixes

- Clearing the plugin log no longer briefly shows a false "Failed to clear logs." error: the Clear button now confirms success immediately and refreshes the view right away
- Genuine clear failures (e.g. expired session or server error) now write a structured diagnostic to the browser console with the HTTP status and error kind, alongside the visible red button feedback, so a real problem is never silent
- Save bar no longer crowds on phones: the unsaved-changes label and Save button now stack on narrow screens, so long translations like the German "Nicht gespeichert" are no longer cut off
- Widescreen films are counted at their real resolution: cinemascope masters like 1920x800 or 1920x1040 are now correctly shown as 1080p instead of 720p in the Codecs tab, decided by whichever axis reaches a resolution class
- The resolution drill-down now lists each file's exact pixel dimensions (e.g. 1920x800) next to its name, readable on desktop and phones
- Chart tooltips work reliably on touch: the first tap on the Trends chart or a Codecs ring now shows and keeps the tooltip instead of flashing it away, and a second tap on the same Codecs segment closes it
- The save confirmation only appears after a real save: reverting a setting back to its original value no longer briefly shows "All changes saved"
- Tested by 5535 unit tests and 320 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.1 - Per-instance library allocation for Arr

- Assign specific Jellyfin libraries to each Radarr/Sonarr instance, so the Arr tab compares an instance only against the libraries it manages
- With two or more instances of a type, each gets a picker in Settings listing only the matching kind of library (movies for Radarr, TV for Sonarr)
- Leave a picker empty to keep it automatic: instances are matched to libraries from their root folders
- Assignments are kept across backup and restore
- Fixes a 4K instance flagging every 1080p film as "not in Radarr"
- Tested by 5499 unit tests and 318 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.0 - Major release for Jellyfin 12.0+

- Books in your library overview: eBook libraries now show their size and file count on the Overview tab and count towards your storage totals, and they're always protected from every cleanup task
- Smarter recommendations: a much bigger model, fairer suggestions for brand-new users, and more variety in your top picks (no more ten near-identical films in a row)
- Recommendations now also learn from franchises/collections, country of origin, collection & folder themes, whether a series is finished or ongoing, writers/creators, top-billed cast, and how rare a genre or studio is in your library (each signal is optional per item, so missing metadata never skews a pick)
- Fresh picks appear between nightly runs, and faster generation on big libraries
- Redesigned Settings, Health and Arr tabs with a live 'reachable' indicator, plus a sticky save bar and unsaved-changes warning
- Better on phones
- Stronger security: API keys are never shown to the browser, backups can leave keys out, and cleanup can never delete or touch anything outside your media libraries
- Safer trash and cleanup: turning retention off really turns it off, trashing a shortcut never removes the file it points to, and Windows shortcut handling is fixed
- More accurate library stats and safer Seerr request cleanup
- More reliable saves and backups (no more rare 'lost save' when antivirus is scanning)
- New end-to-end test suite runs the plugin inside a real Jellyfin 12 server on every change and proves cleanup stays inside your libraries
- Note: your recommendation model retrains from scratch after upgrading, so suggestions settle back in over the next scheduled runs
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v2.1.0.6: Diagnostics for reverse-proxy / WAF-blocked config saves. Added GET /JellyfinHelper/Ping liveness endpoint. Configuration model-binding and validation errors are now logged to the plugin log (source "API", level WARN) instead of silently returning 400. Frontend save handler now classifies errors (network / proxy / server / unauthorized) and surfaces the HTTP status and body snippet to the console, with an automatic Ping follow-up to distinguish "backend unreachable" from "backend reachable, payload rejected". 2325 tests.

v2.1.0.5: Fix StackOverflow on circular symlinks in directory scan. Fix IOException on long trash path names. Added Swedish (sv) language. Exclude Libraries multi-select dropdown. Trash folder browser. Trash path change dialog (move/delete content on path change). Enhanced trash path validation. Upgraded to Jellyfin 10.11.10. 2318 tests.
v2.1.0.4: Fix MissingMethodException for IUserManager.Users.

v2.1.0.3: Add TMDB and Seerr deep links on discovery card flip-back (opens system browser on mobile). Fix 400 Bad Request when submitting discovery requests on Seerr instances with 0-based server IDs. Fix duplicate quality profiles in selection popup for users with multiple root folders. Add graceful error handling for Jellyfin version incompatibility in watch history collection. 2206 tests
v2.1.0.2: Improved Discovery Sidebar Navigation - tab layout can show more than 5 recommendations in one row now. Automatically reloading next recommendation after one was dismissed or requested.
v2.1.0.1: Fix Discovery sidebar navigation - tab is now found dynamically by container index regardless of user-configured tab name, instead of relying on exact text match.

v2.1.0.0: Seerr Discovery - personalized external content recommendations via Overseerr/Jellyseerr with ensemble scoring, one-click request submission, parental rating enforcement, language-based discovery, and Arr library exclusion. 2190 tests.

v2.0.0.3: Instance-based Arr config (legacy removed), persistent language/log-level. Recommendations add audio language & creation date, subtitle language affinity, collection progression boost; meaningful-interaction watched predicates. Centralized popularity scoring, richer training features (31-feature vector), series aggregation, weight schema bump. Neural MLP upgraded to 4-hidden-layer architecture (31→48→24→12→6→1, ~3097 params). Training refactored into TrainingDataBuilder + TrainingFeatureComputer. A/B testing cohort infrastructure with deterministic user bucketing and adaptive sigmoid midpoint. 2124 tests.

v2.0.0.2: Replaced decorative emojis with Material Symbols font icons for consistent cross-platform rendering. Standardized dash punctuation. Fixed subtitle orphan detection to avoid false deletions. 2110 tests.
v2.0.0.1: UI improvement - Recommendations and Watch Activity sections in the Discover tab are now collapsible. Collapsible state is preserved on user switch. 2032 tests.

v2.0.0.0: New Discover tab using an ensemble ML model to provide tailored content recommendations. This update also introduces granular activity tracking and improved system cleanup for uninstallation of this plugin. 2032 tests.

v1.2.1.0: Statistics refactored to use Jellyfin MediaStream metadata (replaces filename parsing). Dynamic range detection (HDR10, HDR10+, Dolby Vision, HLG, SDR). Extended resolution classification (8K, 1440p, SD). Differentiated audio codecs (TrueHD Atmos, DTS-X, DTS-HD MA, EAC3 Atmos). Donut chart enhancements with dynamic range visualization. Library Insights in Trends tab (top-10 largest directories, recently added/changed items, per-library size breakdown with 15-min cache). Performance improvement via per-item video stream caching. Documentation updated.
